nodes.name: Fact18VariancePerturbationBound
nodes.rationale: Paper Fact 18 (first inequality): the L1 distance between N(mu,sigma^2) and the variance-scaled N(mu,sigma^2(1+delta)) is at most 10*delta. Lean states exactly this with 0 <= delta <= 1/2.

nodes.name: Lemma35L1NormGeSetIntegral
nodes.rationale: Despite the file name, the statement is the generic measure-theory fact ∫_S |f| ≤ L1Norm f (set-integral of |f| ≤ full L1 norm). This is NOT paper Lemma 35 (which is ‖N(0,1)-N(0,1+ε)‖₁ ≥ ε/100). A standard monotonicity helper, not a paper result.

nodes.name: M0OfMixtureDifferenceIsZero
nodes.rationale: M_0(F)=M_0(F')=1 and their difference is 0. Immediate consequence of the moment definition M_i(F)=E[x^i] (the 0-th moment of a probability density is 1); the paper does not state this as a result, so classified helper.

nodes.name: MomentIntegralLinearity
nodes.rationale: Linearity step: integral of a degree-6 polynomial times a signed combination density equals the corresponding linear combination of its raw moments. Proof step in the Lemma 9 polynomial-pairing argument, not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: PinskerDataProcessingInequality
nodes.rationale: Data-processing inequality for KL divergence under the two-cell partition {A, Aᶜ}. Standard information-theory fact (a Mathlib-gap filler) supporting the Pinsker/KL machinery behind Fact 18; the paper does not state a data-processing inequality, so classified helper.

nodes.name: PinskerL1FromTwoPoint
nodes.rationale: Pinsker's inequality: ‖f-g‖₁ ≤ √(2·KL(f‖g)) for densities. A standard information-theory fact (the L1/KL bound underlying Fact 18); the paper invokes it but does not state it as one of its numbered results.

nodes.name: PinskerScheffeIdentity
nodes.rationale: Standard Scheffe identity: for two densities, ||f-g||_1 = 2*(integral over {f>g} of f minus g). Not stated as a result in this paper (no Scheffe/Pinsker statement in the .tex); used as infrastructure for TV-distance lower bounds.

nodes.name: PinskerTwoPointBound
nodes.rationale: Two-point Pinsker inequality (p-q)² ≤ ½(p·log(p/q) + (1-p)·log((1-p)/(1-q))). Standard information-theory inequality (the Bernoulli-pair case of Pinsker) underlying the ‖F1-F2‖ ≤ √(2 KL) bound the paper uses inside Fact 18; the paper does not state Pinsker as a result, so classified helper.

nodes.name: SublemmaBinomialCoefficientBound
nodes.rationale: Standard combinatorial bound C(j,i) <= 2^k for i<=j<=k; not a paper result.

nodes.name: SublemmaMixtureMomentLinearity
nodes.rationale: Moment linearity for a 2-component mixture: M_i(F) = w₁·M_i(F₁) + w₂·M_i(F₂). Immediate consequence of the moment definition M_i(F)=E_{x∼F}[x^i] together with the mixture density F = w₁N₁ + w₂N₂ (linearity of the integral); the paper does not state this as a separate result, so classified helper.

nodes.name: SublemmaMomentOfSumOfIndependents
nodes.docstring:
For two independent Gaussians `X ∼ N(μ_X, σ_X²)` and `Z ∼ N(μ_Z, σ_Z²)`, the `i`-th
raw moment of the sum `X + Z` (whose distribution is `N(μ_X + μ_Z, σ_X² + σ_Z²)`)
equals the binomial convolution of the marginal raw moments:

  `M_i(X + Z) = Σ_{j=0}^{i} C(i, j) · M_{i-j}(X) · M_j(Z)`.
nodes.rationale: Moments of a sum of two independent Gaussians equal the binomial convolution of their moment sequences. This is the 'key observation' the paper cites in prose for Lemma 6 ('moments of F and F_alpha(F) are related by a simple linear transformation'), but it is not stated as a numbered result; it is a supporting identity, so helper.

nodes.name: TailBoundExpDecay
nodes.rationale: Standard analytic fact: A*exp(-1/(c*eps^2)) <= eps^N for eps below a threshold (exponential beats any polynomial). Used to discard exponentially-small tails (Lemma 9 sketch / Lemma 29), not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: six_moments_suffice
nodes.docstring: **Six-moments-suffice (qualitative limit).**
nodes.rationale: Qualitative ('six moments suffice') form of Theorem 4: if two nondegenerate two-Gaussian mixtures agree on all of their first six raw moments, they are equal up to component relabelling (MixtureRelabelEquiv). This is the identifiability statement that Theorem 4 is the robust quantitative version of (Section 3 intro: 'one of the first six raw moments will differ'); proved here as a direct corollary of theorem_4_polynomially_robust_identifiability. Linked to the Theorem 4 anchor at lower confidence because the paper states only the quantitative form as a numbered result, not this exact contrapositive.

nodes.name: theorem_4_polynomially_robust_identifiability
nodes.docstring: **Theorem 4 (Moitra--Valiant, Polynomially Robust Identifiability).**
nodes.rationale: Paper Theorem 4 verbatim: ∃ c>0 s.t. for every ε-standard pair (F,F') with ε<c, max_{i≤6} |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ≥ ε^67. The Lean statement matches exactly — same existential constant c>0, same ε-standard hypothesis (EpsilonStandardPair F F' ε), and the conclusion ∃ i∈{1,..,6}, |M_i(F)-M_i(F')| ≥ ε^67 (max≥ encoded as ∃ i with that index in {1..6}).

nodes.name: AnalyticIFTSimpleZeroBranch
nodes.docstring:
**Prior work** (real-analytic Implicit Function Theorem; Krantz–Parks 2002,
*The Implicit Function Theorem*, Ch. 6).

For a parametrized family `f : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ` that is jointly continuous together
with its partial `x`-derivative `D : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ` (i.e. `D (c, x)` is the value
of `(∂/∂x) f(c, ·) x`), if at parameter `c = 0` there is a *simple* zero
`x₀` (meaning `f(0, x₀) = 0` and `D(0, x₀) ≠ 0`), then for all sufficiently
small `|c|` there is a continuous local branch `φ(c)` of zeros of `f(c, ·)`
with `φ(0) = x₀`, and the simple-zero property `D(c, φ(c)) ≠ 0` is preserved.

Moreover the branch is **locally unique**: there is a neighbourhood radius
`ε > 0` such that for every `|c| < δ`, `φ(c)` is the ONLY zero of `f(c, ·)`
within distance `ε` of `x₀`. This local-uniqueness clause is an intrinsic part
of the textbook real-analytic Implicit Function Theorem — the implicit solution
of `f(c, x) = 0` near `(0, x₀)` is, by construction, the unique solution in a
fixed product neighbourhood `{|c| < δ} × {|x − x₀| < ε}` (Krantz–Parks 2002,
*The Implicit Function Theorem*, Thm 6.1.2: existence AND uniqueness of the
implicit function on a product neighbourhood).

This is the textbook real-analytic IFT in 1 parameter / 1 unknown.
nodes.rationale: External prior work taken as an AXIOM (is_axiom=true): the real-analytic Implicit Function Theorem for a simple zero of a one-parameter family (Krantz–Parks 2002, Ch. 6), used in the Proposition 7 perturbation argument. Standard textbook input, not a Moitra–Valiant numbered result.

nodes.name: AnalyticParameterFamilySimpleZeroGenericity
nodes.rationale: External prior work taken as an AXIOM (is_axiom=true): the classical real-analytic genericity fact (Krantz–Parks, 'Real Analytic Functions', Ch. 4) that the non-simple-zero parameter locus of an analytic one-parameter Gaussian family is countable. Supports the 'perturb to make variances distinct / zeros simple' step of Proposition 7 / Lemma 9; standard input, not a Moitra–Valiant numbered result.

nodes.name: HummelGidasZeroCount
nodes.rationale: External prior work taken as an AXIOM (is_axiom=true): Theorem 8 of Moitra–Valiant, itself Thm 2.1 of Hummel–Gidas [13] — a bounded analytic f with n zeros, convolved with N(0,σ²), has at most n zeros. The Lean axiom adds the (paper-faithful) boundedness hypothesis. Classified scaffolding because it is an imported external result asserted without proof; the paper anchor is Theorem 8.

nodes.name: ConvolveWithGaussianBounded
nodes.rationale: Convolution of a continuous bounded function with a Gaussian is bounded. Standard analysis fact (boundedness preserved under Gaussian smoothing) used in the heat-equation/deconvolution machinery; not a paper-stated result, so classified helper.

nodes.name: Corollary24
nodes.rationale: Paper Corollary 24: any centered Gaussian N(0,sigma^2,x) evaluated at |x| >= r is at most 1/(r*sqrt(2pi)). Lean: for r>0, mean=0 Gaussian, r<=|y| implies density y <= 1/(r*sqrt(2pi)) (uniform over sigma^2>0). Same statement.

nodes.name: DerivativeBoundOfSignedCombination
nodes.rationale: Uniform bound |deriv S.density| <= 4/eps^12 for <=4 components with coefficients <=1 and variances >= eps^12. The slope bound m feeding Claim 17's tent-area lower bound (Lemma 9); a proof-step estimate, not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: DistinctVariancePerturbationExists
nodes.docstring:
**Existence of a distinct-variance perturbation threshold.**

If `S` has `k = S.components.length ≥ 1` components, then there is `δ₀ > 0` such
that for every `δ` with `0 < δ < δ₀` the perturbed combination
`variancePerturb S δ _` has pairwise-distinct variances (the list of `varSq`
values is `Nodup`) and every component variance is strictly positive.
nodes.rationale: Existence of a perturbation threshold making all component variances distinct and positive. Realizes the parenthetical 'we can always perturb the Gaussians by negligibly small amounts so as to apply Proposition 7' remark; an existence/genericity helper, not a stated result.

nodes.name: Fact18GaussianL1FromKL
nodes.rationale: Despite the file name, this proves L1 <= sqrt(2 * KL) for two Gaussians — Pinsker's inequality, a standard information-theoretic fact used as an intermediate step toward Fact 18. The paper does not state Pinsker as a numbered result, so this is a helper, not a link to Fact 18 (the Fact 18 L1<=10delta bounds are linked at Fact18GaussianMeanShiftL1Bound / the variance-shift file).

nodes.name: Fact18GaussianMeanShiftL1Bound
nodes.docstring:
Fact 18 (mean-shift form, Appendix 9.2 of Moitra–Valiant).

For every real `μ`, every real `δ`, and every `σ² ∈ [1/2, 3/2]`, the `L¹` distance
between two Gaussians of the same variance whose means differ by `δ` is bounded
above by `10 · |δ|`:

  `‖N(μ, σ²) − N(μ + δ, σ²)‖₁ ≤ 10 · |δ|`.
nodes.rationale: Proves ‖N(μ,σ²)−N(μ+δ,σ²)‖₁≤10|δ| on σ²∈[1/2,3/2] — a δ-shift variant, NOT the paper Fact 18 mean-shift inequality (which shifts by σδ). Kept as helper to avoid a mismatched link.

nodes.name: Fact18GaussianVarianceShiftL1Bound
nodes.rationale: Reparameterized variance-shift bound with constant 20 and variances in [1/2,3/2]; differs from Fact 18 (printed constant 10), so kept as helper. Canonical Fact 18 link is Fact18VariancePerturbationBound.

nodes.name: Fact18KLBoundMeanPerturbation
nodes.rationale: KL(N(μ,σ²)‖N(μ+σδ,σ²))=δ²/2 — a computation inside the Fact 18 proof, not one of the paper-stated Fact 18 inequalities.

nodes.name: Fact18KLBoundVariancePerturbation
nodes.rationale: KL(N(μ,σ²) ‖ N(μ,σ²(1+δ))) ≤ 50δ² for δ ∈ [0,1/2]. This corresponds to the variance-case KL step inside the Fact 18 proof, where the paper instead establishes the sharper KL = -½ln(1+δ)+δ/2 ≤ δ²/4. Because the Lean bound constant (50) differs from the paper's stated δ²/4, it is the formalization's own looser KL estimate (a proof step toward Fact 18), not an exact statement match, so classified helper.

nodes.name: FinitenessOfSignedGaussianZeros
nodes.docstring:
**Finiteness of the zero set of a nonzero signed Gaussian combination.**

If `S.density` is not identically zero, then its zero set is finite; equivalently
`zeroCount S.density < ⊤`.
nodes.rationale: If a signed Gaussian combination is not identically zero then its zero set is finite (zeroCount < ⊤). A proof-step fact (analyticity ⇒ isolated zeros) underpinning the Proposition 7 zero-count argument; not separately stated in the paper, so classified helper.

nodes.name: FirstReductionCountNonDecrease
nodes.docstring:
**First reduction, count non-decrease under a single-coefficient
perturbation.**

Let `S` have `k ≥ 1` components, a nonzero coefficient, `S.density ≢ 0` and
finitely many real zeros, and fix an index `i₀` with `a_{i₀} ≠ 0`. Then there is
a sign `s ∈ {+1, -1}` and a threshold `ε₀ > 0` such that for every `ε ∈ (0, ε₀)`,
if all zeros of `S_ε := coeffPerturbSub S i₀ (s·ε)` are simple, then the number of
distinct real zeros does not decrease:
`zeroCount S.density ≤ zeroCount (coeffPerturbSub S i₀ (s·ε)).density`.
nodes.rationale: Count-non-decrease under a single-coefficient perturbation: zeroCount of the perturbed combination is ≥ that of the original. This is an internal step of the Proposition 7 proof reduction (the paper's parenthetical 'we can always perturb the Gaussians ... by negligibly small amounts so as to apply the proposition'), not a separately stated paper result, so classified helper.

nodes.name: FirstReductionSimpleZeros
nodes.rationale: First reduction in the Proposition 7 / Lemma 9 proof: an arbitrarily small coefficient perturbation makes all zeros simple while not decreasing the zero count. This realizes the paper's parenthetical 'we can always perturb the Gaussians ... so as to apply the proposition' (Lemma 9 sketch), but is not itself a numbered result; helper.

nodes.name: FormalGaussianAnalyticZeroCountInduction
nodes.rationale: Induction engine for Prop 7 (≤2(k-1) zeros); proof step, not the canonical Prop 7 statement (see Proposition7ZeroCount).

nodes.name: FormalGaussianNontriviality
nodes.rationale: Nontriviality: a linear combination of k Gaussian exponentials with pairwise-distinct variances and a nonzero coefficient is not identically zero (∃ x with value ≠ 0). Proof-step fact used inside the Proposition 7 zero-count induction; not separately stated in the paper, so classified helper.

nodes.name: FormalGaussianTailEnvelope
nodes.rationale: Tail-envelope property of a signed combination of Gaussians with distinct positive variances: for x beyond +/- thresholds the sum has constant sign and is bounded below by a single dominant Gaussian envelope. Internal Step-1 machinery (paper Sec 6.1) for the Proposition 7 zero-count argument; not a paper-stated result.

nodes.name: FormalToNormalizedBridge
nodes.rationale: Representation bridge: rewrites a bare-exponential Gaussian combination (c_i, nu_i, w_i) as an equivalent SignedGaussianCombination with matching density and nonzero-coefficient structure. Notation/plumbing, not a paper result.

nodes.name: GaussianDensityDerivBound
nodes.rationale: Gaussian density is differentiable with |deriv|≤1/σ². A regularity/derivative bound used by the tent-area (Claim 17) style arguments; the paper does not state it as a result.

nodes.name: GaussianL1LowerBoundCombinedGap
nodes.docstring:
Combined-gap L¹ lower bound (Lemma 5 Case 2b, Branch L linchpin).

There is an absolute constant `C₀ > 0` such that for all means `μ, μ'` and variances
`σ², σ'² ∈ [1/2, 3/2]`,

  `max(min |μ − μ'| 1, |σ² − σ'²|) / C₀ ≤ ‖N(μ,σ²,·) − N(μ',σ'²,·)‖₁`.

The `min |μ − μ'| 1` cap is necessary: `‖·‖₁ ≤ 2` always, so a bare `|μ − μ'|` is unbounded.
Since `|σ² − σ'²| ≤ 1` automatically for variances in `[1/2, 3/2]`, the variance coordinate
needs no cap. The proof uses the odd(mean-shift)/even(variance-shift) orthogonality: on a
far-right band `[2,3]` both perturbations raise the density, so the L¹ integrand dominates
each single-coordinate contribution separately (no reverse-triangle cancellation).
nodes.rationale: Two-single-Gaussian combined-gap L¹ lower bound max(min|μ-μ'|1,|σ²-σ'²|)/C₀ ≤ ‖N(μ,σ²)-N(μ',σ'²)‖₁ (the Case 2b 'Branch L' linchpin per docstring). The paper does not state this single-Gaussian inequality as a numbered result; it is an internal step toward Lemma 5 / Lemma 38, so classified helper. (Lemma 38 is the analogous WEIGHTED two-Gaussian bound and is the closest paper anchor, but the statements differ — unweighted vs weighted, and a different gap exponent — so this is not a genuine statement match.)

nodes.name: GaussianZeroCountInductiveStepProof
nodes.rationale: Inductive step (k → k+1) of the Proposition 7 zero-count induction: from the ≤2(k-1)-zeros hypothesis for k Gaussians, derive ≤2k zeros for k+1 (via the heat-equation / Theorem 8 add-a-Gaussian argument). This is the induction step internal to the proof of Proposition 7 ('Proven by induction on k using Theorem 8'), not a separately stated paper result, so classified helper. Proposition7ZeroCount carries the Prop 7 link.

nodes.name: HalfGaussianMomentBound
nodes.docstring:
**Prior work** (Moitra-Valiant 2010, supporting Lemma 29 via Claims 27, 28
on page 29): the j-th absolute moment of a centred Gaussian density,
integrated over the half-line `[a, ∞)`, admits a polynomial-times-exponential
upper bound for j ≤ 6.

For some absolute `K_27 > 0`, for every `σ² ∈ (0, 1]`, every `a > 0`, and every
`j ∈ {0, …, 6}`,

  `∫_{u ∈ Set.Ici a} u^j · (1/√(2π σ²)) · exp(-u²/(2σ²)) du
    ≤ K_27 * ((a^j + √σ² ^ j + 1) / a) * exp(-(a²)/(2σ²))`.

This subsumes the Mills-ratio bound (j = 0) and the half-Gaussian polynomial
moment recurrence (j ≥ 1).
nodes.rationale: Half-line (∫ over [a,∞)) tail-moment bound for a centred Gaussian, j ≤ 6 (docstring: 'supporting Lemma 29 via Claims 27, 28'). This is an intermediate ingredient toward Lemma 29 (which bounds ∫_{|x|≥2/ε} x^i N(μ,σ²)), not Lemma 29's stated inequality itself, and the paper states the underlying integral identities as Claims 27/28 rather than this packaged bound — so classified helper.

nodes.name: HurwitzGaussianPerturbationSimpleZeroPreservation_param
nodes.docstring:
**Parametrized region (b)** (route (ii)): the same conclusion as
`HurwitzGaussianPerturbationSimpleZeroPreservation`, but with every floor / region /
threshold supplied EXTERNALLY rather than computed internally.  This exposes a
`c`-independent threshold `min v_th1 v_th2` so that a band-uniform caller can feed
banked uniform floors and obtain a single threshold valid for the whole band.

The combinatorial core (zero-cover + `hgp_R3Local` machinery) is `c`-independent given:

* `Kbig` — the outer perturbation region `Icc (b-δ) (b'+δ) \ Ioo (μ_k-δ/2) (μ_k+δ/2)`
  (supplied as `hKbig_eq`);
* `ε₂` — the cover radius for the zero neighbourhoods, with `ε₂ ≤ δ/8`, `ε₂ ≤ 1`, and the
  derivative-continuity fact `hderiv_lb` (`|deriv g x_j|/2 ≤ |deriv g x|` on each
  `Icc (x_j - ε₂) (x_j + ε₂)`), all of which depend only on `g` (not on any band slice);
* the external derivative floor `ε₁` with `hε₁_le : ε₁ ≤ |deriv g x_j|` at every zero;
* the external value floor `g_lb` with `hg_lb_spec` on the zero-free part
  `(Icc b b' \ Ioo (μ_k-δ) (μ_k+δ)) \ ⋃_{g x_j = 0} Ioo (x_j-ε₂) (x_j+ε₂)`;
* the two perturbation-decay thresholds `v_th1, v_th2` (from
  `SublemmaSmallPerturbationDerivOnZeroNbhds` with floor `ε₁/2` and
  `SublemmaSmallPerturbationOnZeroNbhds` with floor `g_lb`), supplied with their specs.

The returned threshold is exactly `min v_th1 v_th2`, built from the EXTERNAL floors.
nodes.rationale: Parametrized variant of the region-(b) simple-zero-preservation result with all thresholds supplied externally; proof-internal construction, not a paper-stated result.

nodes.name: HurwitzGaussianPerturbationTailDominance_uniform
nodes.docstring:
**Uniform-threshold tail dominance.**  The tail-comparison thresholds `vL, vR`
returned by `tail_left_dom`/`tail_right_dom` depend ONLY on the envelope scalars
`(b, b', a, a', s, s', a_k, μ_k)`, not on the function `g`.  So a SINGLE threshold
`v₀ = min vL vR > 0` works for EVERY `g` sharing the envelope: this exposes that
uniformity by quantifying `g` (and its per-`g` envelope clauses `hL`, `hR`) INSIDE the
existential.  This is the band-uniform region-(a) tail containment consumed by the
diagonal assembly.
nodes.rationale: Uniform-threshold variant of the tail-dominance plumbing; proof-step helper, not a paper result.

nodes.name: Lemma29Assembly
nodes.docstring:
Lemma 29 (full statement, packaged as assembly). For every `μ ∈ ℝ`, every variance
`σ² ∈ (0, 1]`, every `ε ∈ (0, 1]`, and every integer `i ∈ {0, …, 6}`, assuming
`|μ| ≤ 1/ε`,

  `|∫_{|x| ≥ 2/ε} x^i · (1/√(2π σ²)) · exp(-(x-μ)²/(2σ²)) dx|
    ≤ K29 · (1/ε^i) · exp(-1/(2 ε²))`

for an absolute constant `K29 > 0`.
nodes.rationale: Lemma 29 (tail of central moment integrals): for σ²≤1, |μ|≤1/ε, the tail raw-moment integral ∫_{|x|≥2/ε} x^i N(μ,σ²,x) dx = O((1/ε^i)·exp(-1/(2ε²))). Lean states exactly this with an explicit absolute constant K_29 for i≤6.

nodes.name: Lemma29BinomialAbsExpansionBound
nodes.docstring:
Elementary expansion bound: for every `μ, u : ℝ` and every `i : ℕ`,

  `|u + μ|^i ≤ 2^i * (|u|^i + |μ|^i)`.
nodes.rationale: Elementary inequality |u+mu|^i <= 2^i*(|u|^i+|mu|^i). A binomial/triangle estimate used in the Lemma 29 tail-moment proof; standard fact, not a paper-stated result.

nodes.name: Lemma29ChangeOfVariablesTranslation
nodes.docstring:
Change-of-variables for translation on the real line, specialised to the form needed
by Lemma 29. For every Lebesgue-measurable `f : ℝ → ℝ`, every shift `μ ∈ ℝ`, and every
Lebesgue-measurable set `S ⊆ ℝ`,

  `∫ x in S, f (x - μ) = ∫ u in {u : ℝ | u + μ ∈ S}, f u`,

i.e. substituting `u := x - μ` rewrites a set integral over `S` (with integrand
`f (x - μ)`) as a set integral over `S - μ = {u : ℝ | u + μ ∈ S}` (with integrand
`f u`). Uses translation-invariance of Lebesgue measure on `ℝ`.

Specialised to `S := {x : ℝ | 2/ε ≤ |x|}` and `f u := |u + μ|^i · (1 / √(2π σ²))
  · exp(-u² / (2 σ²))`, this rewrites the Gaussian tail integral so that the
Gaussian is centred at `0` and the moving piece `|x|^i` becomes `|u + μ|^i`.
nodes.rationale: Translation change-of-variables for Lebesgue set integrals, a proof step inside Lemma 29 (the paper just writes the substitution u = x - mu). Standard measure-theory fact, not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: Lemma29SigmaAwareTailMomentStandardNormal
nodes.docstring:
Sigma-aware tail moment bound for the centred Gaussian `N(0, σ²)`, for moment orders
`0 ≤ j ≤ 6`. There is an absolute constant `K27 > 0` such that for every variance
`σ² ∈ (0, 1]`, every `a > 0`, and every integer `j ∈ {0, …, 6}`,

  `∫_{a}^{∞} u^j · (1 / √(2π σ²)) · exp(-u² / (2 σ²)) du`
    `≤ K27 · (a^{j-1} + σ^{j-1}) · exp(-a² / (2 σ²))     for j ≥ 1`,

and for `j = 0` the Mills-ratio bound

  `∫_{a}^{∞} (1 / √(2π σ²)) · exp(-u² / (2 σ²)) du ≤ K27 · exp(-a² / (2 σ²))`.

To avoid the `j - 1` underflow on `ℕ` when `j = 0`, we state the unified bound
using a real-valued polynomial-in-`a, σ` upper bound `(a^j + σ^j + 1) / a`
(times `exp(-a²/(2σ²))`) that subsumes both cases. Concretely, we package it as:

For some absolute `K27 > 0`, for every `σ² ∈ (0, 1]`, every `a > 0`, and every
`j ∈ {0, …, 6}`,

  `∫_{u ∈ Set.Ici a} u^j · (1 / √(2π σ²)) · exp(-u² / (2 σ²)) du
    ≤ K27 * (a^j + Real.sqrt σ²^j + 1) / a * Real.exp (-(a^2) / (2 * σ²))`.

This single statement implies both the `j ≥ 1` polynomial bound (multiply through
by `a`) and the `j = 0` Mills-ratio bound (specialise to `j = 0`, the `(a^0 + σ^0 + 1)/a
= 3/a` factor is harmless against `exp(-a²/(2σ²))`).
nodes.rationale: Half-line (∫ over [a,∞)) tail-moment bound for the centred Gaussian N(0,σ²), j ≤ 6 (same statement as HalfGaussianMomentBound, to which it is definitionally equal). This is the σ-aware ingredient toward Lemma 29 (which bounds the full ∫_{|x|≥2/ε} x^i N(μ,σ²)), not Lemma 29's stated inequality, and the paper expresses the underlying integrals via Claims 27/28 — so classified helper.

nodes.name: Lemma29TailMomentVarLeTwo
nodes.rationale: Looser variant of Lemma 29 (sigma^2<=2, decay exp(-1/(4eps^2))) than the printed bound; kept as helper. Canonical Lemma 29 link is Lemma29Assembly.

nodes.name: Lemma5Case1Assembly
nodes.rationale: Assembles 'Case 1' of the Lemma 5 case analysis (a poly(ε) L¹ lower bound when one component's variance/mean is sufficiently separated). Lemma 5 itself is the existence-of-α statement D(F_α(F),F_α(F')) = Ω(ε⁴) with smallest variance ≥ ε^{12}; this decl is one case of its proof (the paper's 'first case to consider'), not the lemma's stated conclusion — classified helper.

nodes.name: Lemma5Case1DerivBoundOnDiff
nodes.rationale: Differentiability and a uniform derivative bound for the difference of two deconvolved mixtures (Case 1 of the Lemma 5 proof, providing the Lipschitz constant m for the tent-area Claim 17 argument). A proof-step estimate, not a paper-stated result.

nodes.name: Lemma5Case1OffPeakBoundAtMu1
nodes.rationale: Case 1 of Lemma 5's case analysis: both F' components are far (variance or mean) from σ₁²,μ₁, bounding the deconvolved F' density at μ₁ off-peak. An intermediate case-lemma in the proof of Lemma 5, not the numbered statement.

nodes.name: Lemma5Case1PeakBoundAtMu1
nodes.rationale: Proof-step inside Lemma 5 Case 1: a lower bound on the deconvolved density value at mu1 (peak height w1/(sqrt(2pi)*eps^6) after deconvolving comp1's variance down to eps^12). An internal case estimate, not a separately-stated paper result.

nodes.name: Lemma5Case2aAssembly
nodes.rationale: Assembly of Case 2a of the Lemma 5 case analysis (weights mismatched, eps^2 <= |w1-w1'|): produces an alpha with the eps^12 variance floor and the Omega(eps^4)-type TV gap for this case. One internal case of the Lemma 5 proof, not the headline statement (linked at Lemma5DeconvolutionTVGap).

nodes.name: Lemma5Case2bAssembly
nodes.docstring:
Branch L of Case 2b: small weight gap (`|Δw₁| < 48ε³`), deconvolution
`β = σ₁² − 1/2` (post-deconv variances in `[1/2, 3/2]`). The comp2 combined-gap
(`GaussianL1LowerBoundCombinedGap`) supplies an `Ω(ε²)` L¹ signal that beats both
the weight-gap noise `O(ε³)` and the comp1 Fact-18 shift noise `O(ε⁵)`. Concludes
`ε²/(24C₀) ≤ TVDistance`. Extracted into its own declaration for a fresh heartbeat
budget. -/
private lemma cb_branchL_TV
    (F F' : Workspace.Types.GaussianMixture2.GaussianMixture2) (ε β C₀ : ℝ)
    (h₁ : β < min F.comp1.varSq F.comp2.varSq)
    (h₂ : β < min F'.comp1.varSq F'.comp2.varSq)
    (hC₀_pos : 0 < C₀)
    (hCG : ∀ (μ μ' σSq σ'Sq : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σSq) (hσ' : 0 < σ'Sq),
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ σSq → σSq ≤ (3 / 2 : ℝ) →
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ σ'Sq → σ'Sq ≤ (3 / 2 : ℝ) →
        max (min |μ - μ'| 1) |σSq - σ'Sq| / C₀ ≤
          L1Norm (fun x =>
            (⟨μ, σSq, hσ⟩ : GaussianPDF).density x - (⟨μ', σ'Sq, hσ'⟩ : GaussianPDF).density x))
    (hβ : β = F.comp1.varSq - 1/2)
    (hε_pos : 0 < ε) (hε_le_one : ε ≤ 1) (hε_le_1e5 : ε ≤ 1/100000)
    (hε_le_C : ε ≤ 1 / (96 * 96 * C₀))
    (h_std : Workspace.Types.EpsilonStandardPair.EpsilonStandardPair F F' ε)
    (h12 : F.comp1.varSq ≤ F.comp2.varSq)
    (h1'1 : F.comp1.varSq ≤ F'.comp1.varSq)
    (h1'2 : F.comp1.varSq ≤ F'.comp2.varSq)
    (hVF1 : 0 < F.comp1.varSq)
    (hVF1_le1 : F.comp1.varSq ≤ 1) (hVF2_le1 : F.comp2.varSq ≤ 1)
    (hVF'1_le1 : F'.comp1.varSq ≤ 1) (hVF'2_le1 : F'.comp2.varSq ≤ 1)
    (hCase2_var : F'.comp1.varSq - F.comp1.varSq < 16 * ε ^ 10)
    (hCase2_mean : |F'.comp1.mean - F.comp1.mean| < 6 * ε ^ 5)
    (hbranch : |F.weight1 - F'.weight1| < 48 * ε^3) :
    ε^2/(24*C₀) ≤ Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.TVDistance
      (Workspace.Types.MixtureDeconvolution.deconvMixture2 F β h₁)
      (Workspace.Types.MixtureDeconvolution.deconvMixture2 F' β h₂) := by
  set G := Workspace.Types.MixtureDeconvolution.deconvMixture2 F β h₁ with hG
  set G' := Workspace.Types.MixtureDeconvolution.deconvMixture2 F' β h₂ with hG'
  have hG1m : G.comp1.mean = F.comp1.mean := rfl
  have hG1v : G.comp1.varSq = F.comp1.varSq - β := rfl
  have hG2m : G.comp2.mean = F.comp2.mean := rfl
  have hG2v : G.comp2.varSq = F.comp2.varSq - β := rfl
  have hG'1m : G'.comp1.mean = F'.comp1.mean := rfl
  have hG'1v : G'.comp1.varSq = F'.comp1.varSq - β := rfl
  have hG'2m : G'.comp2.mean = F'.comp2.mean := rfl
  have hG'2v : G'.comp2.varSq = F'.comp2.varSq - β := rfl
  have hGw1 : G.weight1 = F.weight1 := rfl
  have hGw2 : G.weight2 = F.weight2 := rfl
  have hG'w1 : G'.weight1 = F'.weight1 := rfl
  have hG'w2 : G'.weight2 = F'.weight2 := rfl
  have hG2v_lo : (1/2:ℝ) ≤ G.comp2.varSq := by rw [hG2v, hβ]; linarith [h12]
  have hG2v_hi : G.comp2.varSq ≤ (3/2:ℝ) := by rw [hG2v, hβ]; linarith [hVF2_le1, hVF1]
  have hG'2v_lo : (1/2:ℝ) ≤ G'.comp2.varSq := by rw [hG'2v, hβ]; linarith [h1'2]
  have hG'2v_hi : G'.comp2.varSq ≤ (3/2:ℝ) := by rw [hG'2v, hβ]; linarith [hVF'2_le1, hVF1]
  have hG1v_lo : (1/2:ℝ) ≤ G.comp1.varSq := by rw [hG1v, hβ]; linarith
  have hG1v_hi : G.comp1.varSq ≤ (3/2:ℝ) := by rw [hG1v, hβ]; linarith [hVF1_le1]
  have hG'1v_lo : (1/2:ℝ) ≤ G'.comp1.varSq := by rw [hG'1v, hβ]; linarith [h1'1]
  have hG'1v_hi : G'.comp1.varSq ≤ (3/2:ℝ) := by rw [hG'1v, hβ]; linarith [hVF'1_le1, hVF1]
  have hG2pos : 0 < G.comp2.varSq := G.comp2.varSq_pos
  have hG'2pos : 0 < G'.comp2.varSq := G'.comp2.varSq_pos
  have hw2_lb : ε ≤ F.weight2 := h_std.eps_le_weight2_F
  have hw1_nn : 0 ≤ F.weight1 := F.weight1_nonneg
  have hw2_nn : 0 ≤ F.weight2 := F.weight2_nonneg
  have hw1_le : F.weight1 ≤ 1 := by linarith [F.weight2_nonneg, F.weights_sum_one]
  have hΔw2_eq : |F.weight2 - F'.weight2| = |F.weight1 - F'.weight1| := by
    have e1 : F.weight2 = 1 - F.weight1 := by linarith [F.weights_sum_one]
    have e2 : F'.weight2 = 1 - F'.weight1 := by linarith [F'.weights_sum_one]
    rw [e1, e2, show (1 - F.weight1) - (1 - F'.weight1) = -(F.weight1 - F'.weight1) from by ring, abs_neg]
  have hΔμ1 : |F.comp1.mean - F'.comp1.mean| < 6 * ε^5 := by rw [abs_sub_comm]; exact hCase2_mean
  have hΔv1 : |F.comp1.varSq - F'.comp1.varSq| < 16 * ε^10 := by
    rw [abs_sub_comm, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith [h1'1])]; exact hCase2_var
  have hinter := h_std.inter_sep_id
  have hε3_le_ε2' : ε^3 ≤ ε^2 := pow_le_pow_of_le_one hε_pos.le hε_le_one (by norm_num)
  have hε5_le_ε2 : ε^5 ≤ ε^2 := pow_le_pow_of_le_one hε_pos.le hε_le_one (by norm_num)
  have hε10_le_ε2 : ε^10 ≤ ε^2 := pow_le_pow_of_le_one hε_pos.le hε_le_one (by norm_num)
  have hε2_le_small : ε^2 ≤ ε * (1/100000) := by
    have : ε^2 = ε * ε := by ring
    rw [this]; exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hε_le_1e5 hε_pos.le
  have hcomp2_gap : ε/2 ≤ |F.comp2.mean - F'.comp2.mean| + |F.comp2.varSq - F'.comp2.varSq| := by
    have hw2gap : |F.weight2 - F'.weight2| < 48*ε^3 := by rw [hΔw2_eq]; exact hbranch
    have hb1 : 48*ε^3 ≤ 48*ε^2 := by linarith [hε3_le_ε2']
    have hb2 : 6*ε^5 ≤ 6*ε^2 := by linarith [hε5_le_ε2]
    have hb3 : 16*ε^10 ≤ 16*ε^2 := by linarith [hε10_le_ε2]
    have hsmall : 118*ε^2 ≤ ε/2 := by
      have : 118*ε^2 ≤ 118*(ε*(1/100000)) := by linarith [hε2_le_small]
      nlinarith [this, hε_pos.le]
    linarith [hinter, hΔμ1, hΔv1, hbranch, hw2gap, hb1, hb2, hb3, hsmall]
  have hmaxgap : ε/6 ≤ max (min |F.comp2.mean - F'.comp2.mean| 1) |F.comp2.varSq - F'.comp2.varSq| := by
    rcases le_or_gt (ε/4) (|F.comp2.varSq - F'.comp2.varSq|) with hv | hv
    · exact le_trans (by linarith) (le_max_right _ _)
    · have hμ : ε/4 ≤ |F.comp2.mean - F'.comp2.mean| := by linarith [hcomp2_gap]
      have hε4_le1 : ε/4 ≤ 1 := by linarith [hε_le_one]
      have hmin : ε/4 ≤ min |F.comp2.mean - F'.comp2.mean| 1 := le_min hμ hε4_le1
      exact le_trans (by linarith) (le_trans hmin (le_max_left _ _))
  have hCG2 := hCG G.comp2.mean G'.comp2.mean G.comp2.varSq G'.comp2.varSq hG2pos hG'2pos
    hG2v_lo hG2v_hi hG'2v_lo hG'2v_hi
  have hd2 : (⟨G.comp2.mean, G.comp2.varSq, hG2pos⟩ : GaussianPDF).density = G.comp2.density :=
    (cb_density_eq G.comp2 hG2pos).symm
  have hd2' : (⟨G'.comp2.mean, G'.comp2.varSq, hG'2pos⟩ : GaussianPDF).density = G'.comp2.density :=
    (cb_density_eq G'.comp2 hG'2pos).symm
  rw [hd2, hd2'] at hCG2
  have hgapeq : max (min |G.comp2.mean - G'.comp2.mean| 1) |G.comp2.varSq - G'.comp2.varSq|
      = max (min |F.comp2.mean - F'.comp2.mean| 1) |F.comp2.varSq - F'.comp2.varSq| := by
    rw [hG2m, hG'2m, hG2v, hG'2v, hβ]
    congr 2
    · ring_nf
  rw [hgapeq] at hCG2
  have hG2diff_lb : (ε/6)/C₀ ≤ L1Norm (fun x => G.comp2.density x - G'.comp2.density x) := by
    refine le_trans ?_ hCG2
    gcongr
  have hG2'_L1 : L1Norm G'.comp2.density = 1 := cb_L1Norm_density_eq_one G'.comp2
  have hwrt := cb_weighted_rev_tri F.weight2 F'.weight2 G.comp2.density G'.comp2.density
    (cb_int G.comp2) (cb_int G'.comp2) hw2_nn
  rw [hG2'_L1, mul_one] at hwrt
  have hw2diff_lb : ε * ((ε/6)/C₀) - 48*ε^3
      ≤ L1Norm (fun x => F.weight2 * G.comp2.density x - F'.weight2 * G'.comp2.density x) := by
    have h1 : ε * ((ε/6)/C₀) ≤ F.weight2 * L1Norm (fun x => G.comp2.density x - G'.comp2.density x) := by
      apply mul_le_mul hw2_lb hG2diff_lb (by positivity) hw2_nn
    have h2 : |F.weight2 - F'.weight2| ≤ 48*ε^3 := by rw [hΔw2_eq]; linarith [hbranch]
    linarith [hwrt, h1, h2, cb_L1Norm_nonneg (fun x => G.comp2.density x - G'.comp2.density x)]
  have hμgap1 : |G.comp1.mean - G'.comp1.mean| < 6*ε^5 := by
    have heq : G.comp1.mean - G'.comp1.mean = F.comp1.mean - F'.comp1.mean := rfl
    rw [heq, abs_sub_comm]; exact hCase2_mean
  have hvgap1 : |G'.comp1.varSq - G.comp1.varSq| < 16*ε^10 := by
    have heq : G'.comp1.varSq - G.comp1.varSq = F'.comp1.varSq - F.comp1.varSq := by
      show (F'.comp1.varSq - β) - (F.comp1.varSq - β) = F'.comp1.varSq - F.comp1.varSq; ring
    rw [heq, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith [h1'1])]; exact hCase2_var
  have hG1diff_ub : L1Norm (fun x => G.comp1.density x - G'.comp1.density x) ≤ 60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10 :=
    cb_comp1_diff_ub G.comp1 G'.comp1 ε hG1v_lo hG1v_hi hG'1v_lo hG'1v_hi hμgap1 hvgap1
  have hsplit := WeightedMixtureL1TriangleSplit F.weight1 F.weight2 F'.weight1 F'.weight2
    G.comp1.density G.comp2.density G'.comp1.density G'.comp2.density
    (cb_int G.comp1) (cb_int G.comp2) (cb_int G'.comp1) (cb_int G'.comp2) hw1_nn
  have hG'1_L1 : L1Norm G'.comp1.density = 1 := cb_L1Norm_density_eq_one G'.comp1
  have hG'2_L1' : L1Norm G'.comp2.density = 1 := cb_L1Norm_density_eq_one G'.comp2
  rw [hG'1_L1, hG'2_L1'] at hsplit
  have hrhs_fun : (fun x => (F.weight1 * G.comp1.density x + F.weight2 * G.comp2.density x)
        - (F'.weight1 * G'.comp1.density x + F'.weight2 * G'.comp2.density x))
      = (fun x => G.density x - G'.density x) := by
    funext x
    rw [GaussianMixture2.density_eq, GaussianMixture2.density_eq, hGw1, hGw2, hG'w1, hG'w2]
  rw [hrhs_fun] at hsplit
  have h2TV : 2 * Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.TVDistance G G'
      = L1Norm (fun x => G.density x - G'.density x) := by
    rw [Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.TVDistance_def,
        Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.L1NormMixtureDiff_def]
    ring
  have hΔw1_le : |F.weight1 - F'.weight1| ≤ 48*ε^3 := le_of_lt hbranch
  have hw1_bound : F.weight1 * L1Norm (fun x => G.comp1.density x - G'.comp1.density x)
      ≤ 60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10 := by
    have hh := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hG1diff_ub hw1_nn
    calc F.weight1 * L1Norm (fun x => G.comp1.density x - G'.comp1.density x)
        ≤ F.weight1 * (60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10) := hh
      _ ≤ 1 * (60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10) := by
          apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hw1_le (by positivity)
      _ = 60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10 := by ring
  have hwgapnoise : |F.weight1 - F'.weight1| * (1 + 1) ≤ 96*ε^3 := by
    rw [show (1:ℝ)+1 = 2 from by ring]; linarith [hΔw1_le, abs_nonneg (F.weight1 - F'.weight1)]
  have hTVchain : ε * ((ε/6)/C₀) - 48*ε^3 - (60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10) - 96*ε^3
      ≤ 2 * Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.TVDistance G G' := by
    rw [h2TV]
    linarith [hsplit, hw2diff_lb, hw1_bound, hwgapnoise]
  have hεC : 96*96*C₀*ε ≤ 1 := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hε_le_C
    nlinarith [hε_le_C, hε_pos.le, hC₀_pos]
  have hval_eq : ε * ((ε/6)/C₀) = ε^2/(6*C₀) := by field_simp
  rw [hval_eq] at hTVchain
  have hε5_le3 : ε^5 ≤ ε^3 := pow_le_pow_of_le_one hε_pos.le hε_le_one (by norm_num)
  have hε10_le3 : ε^10 ≤ ε^3 := pow_le_pow_of_le_one hε_pos.le hε_le_one (by norm_num)
  have hnoise_le : 48*ε^3 + (60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10) + 96*ε^3 ≤ ε^2/(12*C₀) := by
    have hLHS : 48*ε^3 + (60*ε^5 + 320*ε^10) + 96*ε^3 ≤ 524*ε^3 := by
      linarith [hε5_le3, hε10_le3]
    have h524 : 524*ε^3 ≤ ε^2/(12*C₀) := by
      rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
      have hε2pos : 0 < ε^2 := by positivity
      have hkey : 6288*C₀*ε ≤ 1 := by nlinarith [hεC, hC₀_pos, hε_pos.le]
      have hrw : 524*ε^3*(12*C₀) = (6288*C₀*ε) * ε^2 := by ring
      rw [hrw]
      calc (6288*C₀*ε) * ε^2 ≤ 1 * ε^2 := by
            apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hkey hε2pos.le
        _ = ε^2 := by ring
    linarith [hLHS, h524]
  have h2TV_lb : ε^2/(12*C₀) ≤ 2 * Workspace.Types.L1AndTVDistance.TVDistance G G' := by
    have hsplit_half : ε^2/(6*C₀) - ε^2/(12*C₀) = ε^2/(12*C₀) := by field_simp; ring
    linarith [hTVchain, hnoise_le, hsplit_half]
  have hh : ε^2/(12*C₀) = 2 * (ε^2/(24*C₀)) := by field_simp; ring
  linarith [h2TV_lb, hh ▸ h2TV_lb]

/-! ## Main theorem.
nodes.rationale: Assembly of Case 2b (matched-component, small weight gap) of Lemma 5's case analysis, producing an α and an Ω(ε^4)-type TV signal. This is one case-lemma of the proof of Lemma 5, not the numbered Lemma 5 statement.

nodes.name: Lemma5DeconvolutionTVGap
nodes.docstring:
Lemma 5 of Moitra--Valiant: existence of a deconvolution parameter `α`
that simultaneously gives an `Ω(ε^4)` TV gap (conditional on the three
measure-theoretic prior-work hypotheses), keeps every constituent variance
`≥ ε^{12}`, and satisfies `α ≥ -1`. The theorem now exposes a smallness
witness `ε_max > 0` (from the ε-absorption in the variance Taylor step).
nodes.rationale: Paper Lemma 5: for every eps-standard pair there is alpha with TV(F_alpha(F),F_alpha(F')) >= Omega(eps^4) and every deconvolved variance >= eps^12. The theorem states exactly this (K5*eps^4 TV gap, var >= eps^12, alpha < min varSq). Conf < 1 because the Lean version carries explicit prior-work measure-theoretic hypotheses; the existential structure and bounds match the paper statement.

nodes.name: Lemma5LocalizedWeightGapTV
nodes.docstring:
comp2 window-mass bound. With window half-width `h = ε³/64` centred at `μ₁`,
the deconvolved comp2 contributes `≤ ε²/8` mass, because the intra-mixture
separation forces it to be either wide in variance (`ε/4 ≤ varSq`) or far in
mean (`ε/4 ≤ |mean − μ₁|`). -/
private lemma loc_comp2_window
    (G2 : GaussianPDF) (μ₁ ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεsmall : ε ≤ 1/100000)
    (hdisj : ε/4 ≤ G2.varSq ∨ ε/4 ≤ |G2.mean - μ₁|) :
    ∫ x in Set.Icc (μ₁ - ε^3/64) (μ₁ + ε^3/64), G2.density x ≤ ε^2/8 := by
  have hεle : ε ≤ 1 := by linarith
  have hh_pos : 0 < ε^3/64 := by positivity
  rcases hdisj with hvar | hmean
  · -- wide variance: peak density ≤ 1/√(2π·(ε/4))
    have hbound : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (μ₁ - ε^3/64) (μ₁ + ε^3/64),
        G2.density x ≤ 1 / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * (ε/4)) := by
      intro x _
      refine le_trans (loc_density_le_peak G2 x) ?_
      apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by have := hε; positivity)
      apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
      nlinarith [hvar, Real.pi_pos]
    have hwin := loc_window_le G2 μ₁ (ε^3/64) (1 / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * (ε/4))) hh_pos hbound
    refine le_trans hwin ?_
    -- arithmetic: (1/√(2π·(ε/4)))·(2·(ε³/64)) ≤ ε²/8
    have hπ : (1:ℝ) ≤ Real.pi := by nlinarith [Real.pi_gt_three]
    have hge : Real.sqrt (ε/4) ≤ Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * (ε/4)) := by
      apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt; nlinarith [hε.le, hπ]
    have hsqrtε4_eq : Real.sqrt (ε/4) = Real.sqrt ε / 2 := by
      rw [show (ε/4) = ε * (1/2)^2 from by ring, Real.sqrt_mul hε.le, Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]; ring
    have hsqrtε_pos : 0 < Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hε
    have hsqrtε4_pos : 0 < Real.sqrt (ε/4) := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)
    have hstep : 1 / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * (ε/4)) ≤ 1 / Real.sqrt (ε/4) :=
      one_div_le_one_div_of_le hsqrtε4_pos hge
    have hmass_le : (1 / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * (ε/4))) * (2 * (ε^3/64))
        ≤ (1 / Real.sqrt (ε/4)) * (2 * (ε^3/64)) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hstep (by positivity)
    refine le_trans hmass_le ?_
    rw [hsqrtε4_eq]
    have hsqrtε_le1 : Real.sqrt ε ≤ 1 := by
      rw [show (1:ℝ) = Real.sqrt 1 from (Real.sqrt_one).symm]; exact Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hεle
    have hεeq : Real.sqrt ε * Real.sqrt ε = ε := Real.mul_self_sqrt hε.le
    rw [div_div_eq_mul_div, one_mul, div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_div_iff₀ hsqrtε_pos (by norm_num)]
    have hε3 : ε^3 = (ε^2 * Real.sqrt ε) * Real.sqrt ε := by rw [mul_assoc, hεeq]; ring
    have hkey : (ε^2 * Real.sqrt ε) * Real.sqrt ε ≤ (ε^2 * Real.sqrt ε) * 2 :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by linarith) (by positivity)
    rw [hε3]; nlinarith [hkey, hsqrtε_pos, mul_pos hε hε]
  · -- far mean: every window point is at distance ≥ ε/8 from G2.mean
    have hh_le : ε^3/64 ≤ ε/8 := by nlinarith [hε.le, hεsmall, sq_nonneg ε, mul_pos hε hε]
    have hbound : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (μ₁ - ε^3/64) (μ₁ + ε^3/64),
        G2.density x ≤ 1 / (ε/8 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)) := by
      intro x hx
      have hdist : ε/8 ≤ |x - G2.mean| := by
        have hx1 : |x - μ₁| ≤ ε^3/64 := by
          rw [abs_le]; constructor <;> [linarith [hx.1]; linarith [hx.2]]
        have hrev : |x - G2.mean| ≥ |G2.mean - μ₁| - |x - μ₁| := by
          have := abs_sub_abs_le_abs_sub (G2.mean - μ₁) (x - μ₁)
          have heq : (G2.mean - μ₁) - (x - μ₁) = -(x - G2.mean) := by ring
          rw [heq, abs_neg] at this
          linarith
        linarith [hmean, hx1]
      exact loc_density_at_distance G2 (ε/8) (by positivity) x hdist
    have hwin := loc_window_le G2 μ₁ (ε^3/64) (1 / (ε/8 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))) hh_pos hbound
    refine le_trans hwin ?_
    -- arithmetic: (1/(ε/8·√(2π)))·(2·(ε³/64)) ≤ ε²/8.  √(2π) ≥ 2.
    have hsqrt_ge_two : (2:ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) := by
      have h4 : Real.sqrt 4 = 2 := by
        rw [show (4:ℝ) = 2^2 from by norm_num, Real.sqrt_sq (by norm_num)]
      rw [← h4]
      apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt; nlinarith [Real.pi_gt_three]
    have hden_pos : 0 < ε/8 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) := by positivity
    rw [one_div, inv_mul_eq_div, div_le_div_iff₀ hden_pos (by norm_num)]
    -- (2*(ε³/64))*8 ≤ ε² * (ε/8 * √(2π)) ; RHS ≥ ε²·(ε/8·2)=ε³/4 ; LHS = ε³/4. equal-ish.
    have h1 : ε/8 * Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) ≥ ε/8 * 2 := by
      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsqrt_ge_two (by positivity)
    nlinarith [h1, hε.le, mul_pos hε hε, mul_pos (mul_pos hε hε) hε]

/-! ## Main theorem.
nodes.rationale: Case-2a localized weight-gap TV lower bound (eps^2/4) for the deconvolved mixtures under the specific Case-2a hypotheses. This is one internal case of the Lemma 5 proof (assembled at Lemma5Case2aAssembly), not the headline Lemma 5 statement, which is linked at Lemma5DeconvolutionTVGap.

nodes.name: Lemma5LocalizedWeightGapTVNarrow
nodes.rationale: A localized (narrow-window) TV lower bound for Case 2b of Lemma 5's case analysis: the Ω(ε^4) signal from a small weight gap in a tiny interval around μ₁. This is an intermediate case-lemma inside the proof of Lemma 5, not the numbered Lemma 5 statement (D(Fα(F),Fα(F'))≥Ω(ε^4)) itself.

nodes.name: Lemma6DeconvolutionPreservesMoments
nodes.docstring:
Paper's Lemma 6 (Moitra--Valiant). Deconvolution at parameter `α` preserves
moment gaps up to a `k · 2^k · (k-1)!!` multiplicative factor: for two-component
Gaussian mixtures `F`, `F'` whose every constituent variance lies in `[α, 1]`
and `α ≥ -1`, every integer `k ≥ 1` satisfies

  Σ_{i=0}^{k-1} |M_{i+1}(F_α(F)) − M_{i+1}(F_α(F'))|
    ≤ (k · 2^k · (k-1)!!) · Σ_{i=0}^{k-1} |M_{i+1}(F) − M_{i+1}(F')|.

The constant `k · 2^k · (k-1)!!` is the actual achievable constant arising from
the paper's explicit chain `C(j,i) < 2^k` combined with Equation (17).

The hypothesis `h_α_ge : (-1 : ℝ) ≤ α` is essential: without a lower bound on
α, the α < 0 case has deconvolved variances `σ² − α = σ² + |α|` that grow
without bound, breaking the moment estimates. The bound α ≥ -1 keeps the
deconvolved variances controlled (≤ 2) and matches the regime used by the
caller (Lemma 5).

For `k = 6`, the constant evaluates to `6 · 64 · 15 = 5760`.
nodes.rationale: Paper Lemma 6: deconvolution at alpha preserves low-order moment gaps up to a multiplicative factor, for two-component mixtures with all variances in [alpha,1]. Same statement (sum over i of moment-gap of deconvolved <= factor * sum of moment-gap of originals). NOTE: Lean uses the weaker multiplicative constant k*2^k*(k-1)!! in place of the paper's (k+1)!/floor(k/2)!; confidence lowered for the differing (looser) constant. Lean also requires alpha >= -1 (consistent with variances in [alpha,1]).

nodes.name: Lemma9MomentGap
nodes.docstring:
**Lemma 9 (genuine, threshold form).**
There is an absolute constant `K₉ > 0` such that for every `K > 0` there is a
threshold `ε_max > 0` such that for every ε-standard pair and admissible
deconvolution parameter, with each post-deconvolution variance `≥ ε^{12}`,
`α ≥ -1`, `ε ≤ ε_max`, and an `L¹` gap `≥ K·ε⁴`, some moment of order
`i ∈ {1,…,6}` of the deconvolved mixtures differs by at least `K₉·K·ε^{66}`.

The threshold `ε_max` honestly depends on `K`: the Gaussian tail
`exp(-1/(4ε²))` is absolute in `K`, so the bound only holds once ε is small
enough relative to `K` for the (sub-polynomial) tail to be dominated by the
bulk.
nodes.rationale: Lemma 9: from an L1 gap Ω(ε^4) of the deconvolved difference f=Fα(F)-Fα(F') with post-deconvolution variances ≥ ε^12, some i≤6 has a moment gap |M_i(Fα(F))-M_i(Fα(F'))|=Ω(ε^66). The Lean theorem is the threshold (poly-ε) form of exactly this statement.

nodes.name: pow_threshold

Pure power threshold: for `c > 0` and `n ≥ 1`, there is `ε₀ > 0` with
`ε^n ≤ c` for all `0 < ε ≤ ε₀`.

nodes.name: pwPoly
nodes.docstring:
The piecewise test polynomial `∑_{i : Fin 7} C(c i) X^i` (degrees 0..6,
matching the piecewise Markov–Chebyshev pairing's coefficient vector).
nodes.rationale: The test polynomial p(x)=Σ c_i X^i used to build the sign-matching degree-6 polynomial in Lemma 9; a construction, not a paper result.

nodes.name: pwPoly_coeff_le
nodes.rationale: Coefficient bound for pwPoly; realizes the 'bounded coefficients' step but is a mechanical helper, not a stated result.

nodes.name: pwPoly_eval
nodes.rationale: Evaluation lemma for pwPoly; mechanical.

nodes.name: pwPoly_natDegree
